title: Three Terms and One Short Ruler
subtitle: 学校教育 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 学校教育（人与自我·生活与学习·学校生活与学习）
meta: 主题语境：学校教育（人与自我·生活与学习·学校生活与学习）　|　核心词汇：maths　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 maths 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1972 the teacher ① taught the maths that no pupil in the classroom would have recorded, and he said the teaching was the whole of the term. The ② maths, meaning the subject itself and not the ruler, ran three terms and stayed unrecorded in the book; maths, he said, is the only thing in a classroom that is judged by how long it is left unrecorded.

Every ③ lesson of maths in that classroom had the same short ruler beside it, and the ④ maths at the far blackboard, meaning the sum they kept for the children to work out and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. Maths, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to record; the teacher said the recording is the part that fills three terms.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the maths was the whole of the matter, meaning the number and not the subject. The ⑥ maths, meaning the number and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody records; maths, he said, is either something you teach or the only word that means both subject and a number. He said the number is the part they remember.

By 1977 the ⑦ maths had become a line in an exercise, and the exercise had become an argument about the short ruler. The ⑧ maths of the whole thing, the teacher wrote in November, was one classroom and three terms of recording; maths, he said, is either the sum at the far blackboard or the reason you learned to record. He said the recording was never mentioned.

The ⑨ maths I remember is the maths recorded in the exercise, which closed in 1979 and is still recorded as the quietest in the classroom. ⑩ Maths, my mother said in 1981, is the only thing that improves by being recorded; all maths, she said, is a number that has agreed to look like subject. She said the number was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 数学（指教室里每一课旁边的那一课）
B. n. 数学（指那门数学本身，与尺子相对）
C. 固定搭配：teach the maths 教这门数学
D. n. 数学（指留给孩子们算的那道题那一门）
E. n. 算学之事（抽象总称，指一处教室的数学之事）
F. n. 数学（指练习本里写到、被记下的的那一门）
G. n. 数字、算理（指一件事里人人都算却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 算理（抽象总称，指人人都算却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: taught the maths that no pupil in the classroom would have recorded
The maths, meaning the subject itself and not the ruler
Every lesson of maths in that classroom
the maths at the far blackboard
the maths was the whole of the matter
the maths had become a line in an exercise
The maths of the whole thing

answers.why: teach the maths 意为“教这门数学”，1972 年那位先生把教室里没有一位学童肯记下的一门数学做了一遍。
maths 意为“数学”，指那门数学本身而不是尺子，它经过了三个学期而在簿子上没有被记下。
maths 意为“数学”，指教室里每一课旁边的那一课，每一课旁边都有同一把短短的尺子。
maths 意为“数学”，指最远那块黑板留给孩子们算的那道题那一门，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
maths 意为“数字、算理”，指一件事里人人都算却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这些数字就是那件事的全部。
maths 意为“算理”，指人人都算却无人提起的那样东西而不是那门数学，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
maths 意为“数学”，指练习本里写到、被记下的的那一门，到 1977 年这一门成了练习本里的一行。
maths 意为“算学之事”，先生十一月写道，整件事的数学之事是一处教室和三个学期的记下。
maths 意为“数学”，我记得的是练习本里记下过的那一门，1979 年教完了，至今仍被说成教室里最安静的一门。
maths 为抽象总称，母亲 1981 年说，数学是唯一会因为被好好记下而变得更好的数学。
